abstract: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of the bright local Seyfert 1 galaxy IC 4329A obtained with \textit{XRISM}/Resolve, supported by simultaneous \textit{NuSTAR} data and quasi-simultaneous optical/near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Resolve separates the Fe K$\alpha$ line into a narrow core and a broad component exhibiting a red excess. We examined three scenarios for this red excess: (1) a redshifted X-ray broad line region (xBLR), (2) relativistic disk reflection, and (3) an unshifted xBLR partially absorbed by a mildly ionized absorber. All three models reproduce the X-ray spectra equally well. Our optical (H$\beta$) and NIR (Pa$\beta$) spectroscopy shows that the broad lines are redshifted by $v \sim +640\text{--}1050\text{ km s}^{-1}$, close to the solution of the redshifted xBLR model ($v_{\rm shift} = +1700_{-800}^{+1700}\text{ km s}^{-1}$). Motivated by this, we constructed a hybrid model in which the xBLR shares the velocity structure of the optical/NIR BLR and the remaining red excess is attributed to a relativistic disk line, which also provides an acceptable fit. The inferred xBLR radius is $R_{\rm BLR} \sim (3\text{--}6) \times 10^3\ R_g$ ($\sim 12\text{--}22$ light-days). From the narrow Fe K$\alpha$ core in the hybrid model (${\rm FWHM} = 870_{-280}^{+260}\text{ km s}^{-1}$), we estimate a torus distance of $R_{\rm torus} \sim 0.9_{-0.4}^{+1.0}$ pc ($\sim 1100$ light-days), close to the dust sublimation radius. Furthermore, two ultra-fast outflow (UFO) absorption features are identified with $v_{\text{wind}} \sim -0.30c$ and $-0.24c$, both confirmed at $>99\%$ confidence.
hook: XRISM splits the iron line of a Seyfert galaxy and finds two fast winds near 0.3 times light speed.

readout.label: Speed of one ultra-fast outflow, IC 4329A

summary: High-resolution X-ray spectra of IC 4329A separate the iron K-alpha line into a narrow core and a broad part with a red excess. Optical and infrared lines are redshifted too, which favors a hybrid model of broad-line gas plus a relativistic disk line, with a torus about 0.9 parsecs out. Three models fit the X-ray data equally well, so the origin of the red excess is not settled.
title: Origin of the Fe K$\alpha$ red excess in IC 4329A with XRISM and multi-wavelength spectroscopy
